contentBody: **A team converts a LinkedIn post into WhatsApp by simply reducing its word count. What is the most important weakness?**
option.1: The copy may preserve a structure that does not suit WhatsApp behaviour
option.2: The copy may lose keywords required for accurate social-media distribution
option.3: The message may become too short to communicate any meaningful proposition
option.4: The message may require an additional headline before it can be delivered
answerExplanation: Each channel needs a different communication architecture, not just a shorter word count.

contentBody: **A B2B marketer is creating the first email for a problem-aware prospect who does not know the brand. Which structure is strongest?**
option.1: Company credentials → product catalogue → pricing → meeting request
option.2: Customer context → relevant problem → value → low-friction next step
option.3: Product features → competitor weakness → discount → purchase request
option.4: Brand history → market statistics → product portfolio → contact details
answerExplanation: Strong outbound email leads with the customer's situation and a clear, low-friction CTA.

contentBody: **An AI-generated InMail is personalised with the recipient's name and company but still performs poorly. What should be examined next?**
option.1: Whether the message demonstrates relevance beyond superficial identity variables
option.2: Whether the recipient's name appears more frequently throughout the communication
option.3: Whether the company description contains sufficient technical detail about the product
option.4: Whether the message uses the same structure as the highest-performing email campaign
answerExplanation: InMail must answer "why you, why now" with context the reader recognises, not only name and company tags.

contentBody: **Why is an iterative prompt usually stronger than repeatedly asking AI to "make it better"?**
option.1: It narrows the model toward specific weaknesses and desired communication choices
option.2: It increases the probability that AI will generate substantially longer marketing copy
option.3: It prevents the model from changing any words that appeared in the initial response
option.4: It guarantees that the final draft will outperform copy written without generative AI
answerExplanation: Diagnose what failed (generic, wrong audience, too product-heavy), then give directed feedback instead of vague "make it better."

contentBody: **A marketer creates email, WhatsApp and call scripts from one positioning statement. What should remain most consistent?**
option.1: The sentence structure and CTA wording used across each customer interaction
option.2: The central customer value while execution adapts to channel behaviour
option.3: The total amount of product information communicated within every channel
option.4: The communication length so customers receive equivalent detail everywhere
answerExplanation: Same strategic spine; change structure, length, opening, proof, CTA, and tone by channel.

contentBody: **A nurture email sequence has strong open rates but every email repeats essentially the same product argument. What is the primary strategic weakness?**
option.1: The sequence is not progressively resolving different customer questions over time
option.2: The sequence requires more subject-line variation before customer behaviour can improve
option.3: The sequence is likely too short because repeated arguments need greater message frequency
option.4: The sequence should move product information exclusively into sales conversations instead
answerExplanation: Nurture should move from problem relevance through education, differentiation, proof, and action—not repeat the same pitch.

contentBody: **Which AI instruction is most likely to improve a call script for an enterprise seller?**
option.1: "Make the script persuasive and include detailed information about every product capability."
option.2: "Create a short opening, discovery questions, objection routes and one logical next step."
option.3: "Convert the existing marketing email into spoken language while retaining its full argument."
option.4: "Write a complete conversation that the seller can read without deviating from the wording."
answerExplanation: A call script is a conversation framework, not a monologue to read word for word.

contentBody: **AI creates technically accurate copy that feels inappropriate for the channel. Which input was most likely under-specified?**
option.1: The communication context and behaviour expected within the selected channel
option.2: The number of alternative versions that should appear in the initial generation
option.3: The amount of competitor information included before the writing task begins
option.4: The level of vocabulary variation required between consecutive copy alternatives
answerExplanation: Prompts need channel, format, audience, objective, stage, and constraints—not only topic and word count.

contentBody: **A company wants every marketer to apply the same 18 brand-writing rules across hundreds of recurring content tasks. Which approach is most appropriate?**
option.1: Store the reusable workflow in a Skill and provide task-specific context separately
option.2: Rewrite the full instructions manually whenever an individual content request begins
option.3: Connect additional external applications so Claude can infer the desired writing style
option.4: Reduce the guidelines to one tone adjective so marketers retain maximum flexibility
answerExplanation: A Skill encodes repeatable operating rules; prompts handle one-off or varying task context.

contentBody: **An AI draft has excellent tone and structure but contains an unverified claim that the product is "India's fastest platform." What should happen first?**
option.1: Retain the claim temporarily and improve its wording before external verification begins
option.2: Replace "fastest" with "leading" because softer adjectives require less supporting evidence
option.3: Verify the claim against an authoritative source or remove it from the communication
option.4: Ask a second AI model whether the statement appears commercially plausible before publishing
answerExplanation: Editing starts with what is true—unsupported superlatives must be verified or cut, not softened.

contentBody: **A marketer asks AI to shorten a 200-word executive email to 80 words. The result loses the most important evidence. What was missing?**
option.1: An instruction defining which communication elements must survive the compression process
option.2: An instruction requiring greater vocabulary variation across the shortened executive message
option.3: An instruction forcing every original sentence to retain a corresponding shortened sentence
option.4: An instruction preventing the model from changing the paragraph order during the rewrite
answerExplanation: When changing length, specify what must stay (proof, CTA, core message) so compression does not drop essentials.

contentBody: **What is the strongest distinction between a Claude Skill and a connector?**
option.1: A Skill encodes repeatable ways of working, while a connector provides access to tools or data
option.2: A Skill retrieves external company information, while a connector determines editorial tone
option.3: A Skill is intended for B2B workflows, while connectors primarily support consumer marketing
option.4: A Skill creates final marketing assets, while connectors are limited to reading static documents
answerExplanation: Skills tell Claude how to work; connectors reach where information and tools live.

contentBody: **A draft feels recognisably "AI-written" despite having no factual errors. Which editing approach is strongest?**
option.1: Remove visible stylistic patterns while preserving generic claims and overall sentence structure
option.2: Add more unusual vocabulary so the writing differs from common generative-AI vocabulary
option.3: Re-anchor the copy in specific audience context, natural phrasing and concrete evidence
option.4: Replace all punctuation associated with AI writing before evaluating the underlying argument
answerExplanation: Human nuance—real examples, audience fit, and proprietary context—beats surface synonym swaps.

contentBody: **A marketing team has excellent prompts but keeps receiving outdated product information in final copy. Which improvement addresses the root issue most directly?**
option.1: Increase the number of creative variants generated before selecting the final marketing draft
option.2: Ground the workflow in current approved product sources before the copy-generation step
option.3: Add more detailed tone instructions so outdated information becomes easier to identify visually
option.4: Build a longer editorial Skill that rewrites unsupported product information more conservatively
answerExplanation: Connectors and approved sources should feed current facts into the workflow before drafting.

contentBody: **A brand Skill consistently produces clear copy, but every campaign begins to sound almost identical. What is the strongest response?**
option.1: Remove all brand guidance so the model can independently create a new voice each time
option.2: Keep stable brand rules while allowing creative direction to vary by audience and objective
option.3: Add more mandatory sentence templates so variation happens inside a controlled structure
option.4: Replace the Skill with a connector because repetitive writing primarily reflects missing data
answerExplanation: Standardise how you work, not every creative angle—vary brief by audience and campaign goal.

contentBody: **Which workflow best represents effective human-in-the-loop AI content production?**
option.1: AI generates → AI scores → highest score publishes automatically → performance is reviewed later
option.2: Human briefs → AI drafts → evidence is checked → human edits → audience response validates
option.3: Human writes → AI corrects grammar → original draft is restored → marketing team publishes
option.4: AI researches → AI writes → AI fact-checks itself → human approves formatting before release
answerExplanation: The stack ends with human judgment: brief, draft, verify, edit, then publish or test.
